div.div:
On the interconnect
Outer IP 10.0.0.4 → 10.0.1.10, UDP 4789
VXLAN VNI 50001
Inner Eth 50:00:00:04:00:08 → 50:0a:00:00:1b:08
(LEAF-4 router MAC → LEAF-BORDER router MAC)
Inner TTL 63

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 246px; height: 1px; padding-top: 260px; margin-left: 808px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1042px; height: 1px; padding-top: 385px; margin-left: 10px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Where the inner MACs come from: each leaf advertises its host routes as EVPN type-2 with two labels (L2 VNI 10020 + L3VNI 50001), two route targets (65000:10020 + 65000:50001) and a Router MAC extended community. LEAF-BORDER has no VLAN 20, so it uses only the L3 half: a /32 in TENANT1 and LEAF-4's router MAC.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1042px; height: 1px; padding-top: 470px; margin-left: 10px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Cold destination (LEAF-BORDER has no ARP entry for SERVER-11): LEAF-4 has only the 10.30.30.0/24 type-5 route, LEAF-BORDER must ARP, and the first packet is dropped. Once SERVER-11 answers, LEAF-BORDER advertises a /32 type-2 route and every later packet goes straight through.
